holidays.name: National Sour Candy Day
holidays.description: This is a day for puckering up. Treat yourself to something tart and tangy, like sour gummy worms, sugar-dusted strips, or face-scrunching lemon drops. Bonus points if you dare a friend to try the sourest one in the bag.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a staple of July candy calendars.
holidays.funFact: The sour sensation comes from food-safe acids like citric, malic, and tartaric acid. Candy makers often coat the outside in these acids, which is why the first bite hits hardest.

holidays.name: National Caviar Day
holidays.description: Fancy a little luxury on a summer Saturday? This day invites you to enjoy salty, briny fish roe on blinis, crackers, or even a humble potato chip. It's an excuse to feel fancy for a day.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates one of the world's best-known delicacies.
holidays.funFact: True caviar comes from sturgeon, a fish family that has swum the planet since the age of the dinosaurs. Some rare varieties, like Almas caviar from albino sturgeon, rank among the most expensive foods in the world.

holidays.name: World Listening Day
holidays.description: This day asks everyone to stop, hush, and tune in to the sounds around them, from birdsong to city traffic to the hum of the fridge. It's a gentle reminder that listening is a skill worth practicing and that soundscapes are worth protecting.
holidays.origin: The World Listening Project created it in 2010 to honor the birthday of R. Murray Schafer, the Canadian composer who pioneered the study of acoustic ecology.
holidays.funFact: R. Murray Schafer coined the word 'soundscape' to describe the total acoustic environment of a place, and he treated sound as something to be designed and protected.
